Definition
[Incompressibility and Haken manifold] \group 3-manifold topology Source: thurston:page-0082, thurston:page-0083 A surface $S\subset M$, excluding the elementary cases stated in the source, is incompressible if every loop on $S$ bounding a disk in $M-S$ bounds a disk in $S$, and is $\partial $-incompressible if every boundary arc homotopic into $\partial M$ is homotopic in $S$ into $\partial S$. An oriented irreducible compact three-manifold containing such a surface is sufficiently large, or Haken.
